CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of kidney stones

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male presenting for evaluation of kidney stones. He reports sudden onset of severe pain in the right back approximately one week ago while working in the barn moving hay. He initially thought the pain was from the activity but then developed severe symptoms including diaphoresis and nausea, prompting him to see his PCP who ordered a CT scan that revealed a kidney stone. The pain radiated almost to the groin but not completely. Since initial presentation, the pain has recurred a couple of times but does not last as long. Patient denies hematuria and states urine has not appeared darker than usual. He has been straining urine as instructed but has not noticed any stones passed. Denies previous kidney stone history.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Reports diaphoresis and nausea associated with initial pain. Denies hematuria. Denies fever.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Father has had multiple kidney stones.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works with horses and performs farm labor including moving hay.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Normal, no fever. Blood pressure and heart rate normal. Abdominal examination: No tenderness to palpation, no rebound or guarding. CVA tenderness on the right side.

RESULTS
CT scan shows a stone measuring 0.5 centimeters located in the proximal right ureter. No evidence of hydronephrosis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Kidney stone, right proximal ureter, 0.5 cm. Plan includes increased fluid intake to facilitate urination and passage of stone. Prescribed oxycodone 5 mg every 6-8 hours for pain with acetaminophen available for breakthrough pain. Continue urinary straining. Ordered BMP, urinalysis, and urine culture to assess for infection; antibiotics may be prescribed based on urinalysis results. Follow-up in 1-2 weeks. If stone has not passed, will discuss lithotripsy as treatment option.
